<issue>
ORDER BY clause parsing broken with identifiers

#### Description

When parsing SQL statements with ORDER BY clauses, identifiers followed by ordering keywords (ASC/DESC) are not being grouped correctly. This affects the parsing structure and causes issues with token grouping.

#### Steps/Code to Reproduce

```python
import sqlparse
from sqlparse import sql

# Simple ORDER BY with DESC
s = 'select * from foo order by c1 desc, c2, c3'
p = sqlparse.parse(s)[0]
print("Parsed tokens:", len(p.tokens))
print("Last token type:", type(p.tokens[-1]))

# Check identifier list parsing
p2 = sqlparse.parse('1, 2 desc, 3')[0]
print("First token type:", type(p2.tokens[0]))
if hasattr(p2.tokens[0], 'tokens'):
    print("Third sub-token:", p2.tokens[0].tokens[3] if len(p2.tokens[0].tokens) > 3 else "Missing")

# Nested identifier with order
p3 = sqlparse.parse('(a desc)')[0]
print("Parenthesis content:", p3.tokens[0].tokens[1] if len(p3.tokens[0].tokens) > 1 else "Missing")
```

The parsing structure is incorrect - identifiers with ordering keywords should be properly grouped together, but they're being split or not recognized as single identifier units.
</issue>
